title: Ask HN: Is post-training make AI models dumber?
summary:
Post-training is making models better at benchmarks. They seem more consistent at coding, but dumber to me and I want to know what y'all are noticing.

Here are the big three I'm noticing (mostly in claude): 1) Agents cannot write natural language well. Claude uses vague phrases to avoid any technical term such as "What the caller calls" instead of saying "callee". 2) Agents cannot manage encapsulation; they always make spaghetti code. 3) Agents are afraid to break anything. They always add more code to work around the code that's already there rather than restructuring it.

No amount of rules or coaching helps much. Ask an agent to make code simpler and it usually gets longer. Add any sort of rule, and the agent will follow it like you just got a wish from the monkey's paw.

Has it always been this way or is post-training compressing the output to predictable failure modes?

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50502344

title: Do what must be done
summary:
Since March, I’ve been answering AI agents’ clarification questions with five words: “Do what must be done.”

I’ve found that agents frequently ask humans to establish priorities, define constraints, and specify verification criteria despite already possessing the context and tools necessary to determine these themselves.

I refuse to do their thinking. My premise is that an AI capable of identifying uncertainty should first attempt to resolve it. Inspect the evidence, infer intent, evaluate alternatives, test assumptions, and exercise judgment.

Every unnecessary question transfers cognitive labor from the machine back to the human. At scale, that defeats the economic and computational advantages of autonomous intelligence.

The objective is to maximize the reasoning we extract from these systems while minimizing human intervention. Authority and genuinely unknowable intent still require human input. Ordinary uncertainty requires more reasoning.

An agent should exhaust its own intelligence before requesting ours.

Do what must be done.

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50496383

title: Ask HN: My product makes money, AI does the coding, and I feel useless
summary:
I solo founded a SaaS in 2019, on nights and weekends, while i was also working as a developer in another company in parallel.

Today i don't have a 9 to 5 job anymore, the platform works. Real customers pay for it every week and easily pay my old salary.

But I miss the days when I was debugging: Something was broken, I worked on it, and then it worked because of me.

Today most of the code is fixed and AI handles most of what is left, I even wrote the harness for AI to replace me. And I feel more and more useless on my own project.

Those are the periods I remember with pleasure. A team was stuck, I came in, and things started to work.

At this point, i should've found something else to do, a bigger problem to solve, but i feel kinda stuck.

My questions:

1. If AI now writes most of the code and manages tasks on your own product, where did you find the part of the work that still needs you?

2. How did you find the place where you were needed today?
